chunks: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I narrate to you the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' So we said, 'Yes.' He called for a jug containing some water, then placed it in front of him, then bared his arms, then immersed his right palm in it, then said: 'This is how, when the palm is clean.'

Then he scooped and filled it with water, so he placed it upon his forehead, then said: 'In the Name of Allah,' and poured it upon the sides of his beard. Then he passed his hand over his face and the apparent part of his forehead once.

Then he immersed his left hand and scooped a full palmful with it, then placed it upon his right elbow, and passed his palm over his forearm until the water flowed upon the sides of his fingers. Then he scooped a full palmful with his right hand, placed it upon his left elbow, and passed his palm over his forearm until the water flowed upon the sides of his fingers. And he wiped the front of his head and the back of his feet with the remnant of his left [hand] and the remainder of the remnant of his right [hand].

He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah is Odd (One) and Loves the odd, so it would suffice you from the ablution three scoops: one for the face, and two for the two arms. And you wipe the front of your head with the remnant of your right hand, and whatever remains of the remnant of your right hand, [wipe] the back of your right foot. And you wipe the back of your left foot with the remnant of your left hand.'

Zurara said, Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'A man asked Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) about the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he narrated to him similar to that.'

key_terms.الْوَتْر: Odd/One (referring to Allah's oneness and preference for odd numbers in acts of worship)
key_terms.قَعْب: A jug or vessel for water

ai.seo_question: What is the step-by-step procedure for performing wudu according to the Prophet Muhammad as described in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi provides a precise, step-by-step narration of the Prophet’s ablution (wudu) via Imam al-Baqir, highlighting the practical application of the principle that 'Allah is Odd and loves oddness' by utilizing three scoops of water. It establishes a direct chain of transmission linking the Prophet’s practice to Imam Ali and then to Imam al-Baqir, reinforcing the authenticity of this specific ritual sequence in Shia jurisprudence. The narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the minimal yet sufficient requirements for ritual purity.
